Executor

ig-ZEK-yuh-tur -- Latin ex- ('out') plus sequi ('to follow'): the one who follows a plan all the way out. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Executor is a person who carries something out and makes it happen.

A good idea is worthless without an executor willing to do the unglamorous work.

Worked Example

Someone sketches a brilliant plan for a school garden on a napkin; another person orders the soil, books the truck, recruits twelve volunteers, and has the beds planted by April.

The person who takes a plan off the page and makes it actually happen is the executor. Unlike the planner, who supplies the vision, the executor supplies the follow-through.

How Executor Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

doer

doer: someone who actually gets things done

administrator

administrator: a person who manages and carries out operations

agent

agent: one who acts to bring something about

Antonyms

planner

planner: one who designs but does not carry out

bystander

bystander: someone present who takes no part

How Strong Is It? — doer → administrator → executor

doer vs. executor

doer vs. executor: Doer is the plain, informal version of executor -- any hard worker can be called a doer, while an executor is specifically the person responsible for carrying out a particular plan.

administrator vs. executor

administrator vs. executor: Administrator is more official than executor: an executor makes one plan or task happen, while an administrator runs the whole ongoing operation, budgets and staff included.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ex-

prefix — ex-: out, fully (Latin)

root — -secut-/-cut-

root — -secut-/-cut-: to follow (Latin (sequi))

suffix — -or

suffix — -or: one who does the action (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin exsequi meant 'to follow out to the end,' from ex- ('out') and sequi ('to follow') -- an executor is the one who follows a plan all the way out, from the same root sequi that gives us sequence and consequence.

Word Choice

This unit teaches executor in its general sense: the one who makes something happen. Be aware that in law the word has a narrower use -- the executor of a will is the person appointed to carry out its instructions -- which is the same idea of 'carrying out,' applied to a document.
